item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 291135
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Wed Jul 29 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on recently
downgraded Tropical Depression Fausto, located in the Central
Pacific a few hundred miles northeast of the Hawaiian Islands, and
on Hurricane Genevieve, located several hundred miles west-southwest
of the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Summary for Hurricane Genevieve (EP2/EP072026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...GENEVIEVE STILL A MAJOR HURRICANE... As of 11:00 PM HST Tue Jul 28 the center of Genevieve was located near 18.4, -118.4 with movement WNW at 9 mph. The minimum central pressure was 956 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 120 mph.

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Public Advisory Number 21
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Tue Jul 28 2026 
792 
WTPZ32 KNHC 290833
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Genevieve Advisory Number  21
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
1100 PM HST Tue Jul 28 2026
 
...GENEVIEVE STILL A MAJOR HURRICANE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM HST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...18.4N 118.4W
ABOUT 630 MI...1015 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...120 MPH...195 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...956 MB...28.23 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Genevieve was 
located near latitude 18.4 North, longitude 118.4 West. Genevieve is 
moving toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). This general 
motion with a slight increase in forward speed is expected during 
the next several days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 120 mph (195 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Genevieve is a category 3 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale. Some weakening is expected during the next few 
days, but Genevieve is forecast to remain a hurricane through 
Thursday night or early Friday. 
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles
(220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 956 mb (28.23 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Genevieve are affecting portions of the 
Baja California Peninsula and will reach Southern California on 
Wednesday. These swells will persist for the next several days and 
are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current 
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
A depiction of rip current risk for the United States can be found
at: hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Forecast Discussion Number 21
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Tue Jul 28 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 290834
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Genevieve Discussion Number  21
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
1100 PM HST Tue Jul 28 2026
 
The eye of Genevieve is no longer apparent in conventional satellite 
imagery. The center is embedded underneath a central dense overcast 
with very cold cloud top temperatures of -70 to -75 deg C. 
Proxy-visible and infrared satellite images show that northwesterly 
shear is restricting upper-level outflow on the west side of the 
hurricane. Based on the deteriorating satellite presentation and 
decreasing satellite intensity estimates (including a T5.5/102 kt 
Dvorak CI from TAFB), the initial intensity is lowered to 105 kt. 
The 34- and 50-kt wind radii were updated based on a recent ASCAT-C 
pass over the hurricane.
 
Genevieve is moving west-northwestward (285/8 kt) along the 
southwestern periphery of a mid-level ridge centered over the 
southwestern United States and northern Mexico. This steering ridge 
is forecast to strengthen and build westward over the next several 
days, which should keep Genevieve on a west-northwestward heading 
with some increase in forward speed late this week and through the 
weekend. The NHC track forecast is essentially an update of the 
previous one, generally falling between the latest corrected (HCCA) 
and simple (TVCN) consensus aids.

The hurricane is experiencing moderate northwesterly shear that will 
persist for the next 12-24 h while it moves over gradually 
decreasing SSTs. By the time the shear is forecast to relent, 
Genevieve will likely have already crossed the 26 deg C isotherm and 
moved into a somewhat drier environment. The latest intensity 
guidance suggests additional strengthening is unlikely, and the 
updated NHC prediction shows Genevieve weakening through the 
forecast period. The largest downward adjustments to the forecast 
were made in the first 48 h, though NHC still lies on the upper end 
of the guidance. The system is forecast to fall below hurricane 
strength on Friday and become post-tropical at day 4, when the GFS 
and ECMWF indicate that strengthening shear will make it difficult 
for the system to sustain organized convection over sub-24 C waters.
